stories.summary: Net migration to the UK fell to its lowest level excluding the pandemic in nearly 30 years, following tougher government actions amid public backlash over immigration. The drop was largely due to fewer non-EU arrivals . Capitalizing on widespread anti-immigration sentiment, populist parties have surged across Europe, pushing governments to adopt a harsher stance. The UK has tightened visa rules for students and workers, with the Home Secretary saying the government had “restored control” by taking action to “only attract the brightest and best.” But analysts warned of an economic fallout : A center-left think tank executive said reindustrializing the UK requires workers “critical to our industrial strategy,” while a migration expert warned “sustained net emigration” could strain public finances . — Tasneem Nashrulla
